At PAF Reading Program, we believe that reading is a civil right In partnership with schools and families, we provide explicit, systematic, evidence-based literacy instruction that gives every student equitable access to rigorous learning while honoring their home languages and the cultural and linguistic assets they bring to the classroom. Our most recent study (WestEd) demonstrated statistically significant, specific reading growth above national expectations in a California school district, with an additional significant finding for multilingual learners, showing that PAF Reading Program is effective in real-world classroom settings as a research-proven foundational reading skills curriculum. 3

See it Say it Write it Read it Multisensory Instruction The goal is for all students to become confident, competent, curious, and independent readers. What is direct instruction? PAF Reading Program’s teaching philosophy is based on the idea that all beginning learners benefit from direct instruction: curricula taught under teacher supervision with immediate feedback to student responses, modeling of appropriate responses, and continuous assessment of children’s progress. Because PAF Reading Program is taught using the direct instruction model, it allows for differentiated instruction, which is crucial to meet the full range of students’ needs. What is multisensory learning? Unlike conventional programs in which reading, spelling, and handwriting are taught separately, mutisensory reading inctruction combines all three in a comprehensive program so each subject reinforces the others. Phonemic awareness, phonics, decoding, word recognition, vocabulary, spelling, handwriting, and comprehension strategies are taught simultaneously in integrated lessons. 5

Level 23 /r/ Plan Plan the lesson using the Teacher Handbook, Teacher Edition, and the Digital Implementation Guide. 1 Review 5 - 7 mins Review previously taught sounds and nonphonetic words using the Review Pack. 2 Introduce 5 - 10 mins Introduce the new phonogram using the Alphabet Picture Cards. 3 Dictate 10 - 15 mins Dictate the new phonogram using words and sentences provided in the Teacher Handbook. 4 Read 25 mins in small groups Students read from the Skills Books to develop decoding skills, word recognition, and fluency. Students read a chapter in the decodable reader to develop comprehension strategies and vocabulary. 5 Reinforce 5 - 10 mins Reinforce skills with activities from the Skills Book and website. Assess Assess student understanding throughout the lesson by making note of any errors during dictation or reading and use to inform instruction. 9

2 K-2 Foundational Skills Reading Program High Quality Instructional Materials Supplemental Materials Aprendo Leyendo decodable chapter books provide additional, structured opportunities for students to practice decoding and build fluency in Spanish while developing parallel skills in English. The decodable texts can be incorporated into independent reading, partner work, or small-group instruction to reinforce skills and support continued practice with connected text. This approach supports access to grade-level content while developing academic language, comprehension, and oral language across both languages. • Authentic Spanish Foundational Reading Built on the same structured literacy approach as PAF Reading, designed for the unique sounds and spelling patterns of Spanish. • Same Methodology/Parallel Structure, Easy Implementation Aprendo Leyendo and PAF Reading share the same lesson structure and routines. Use them alone or together in 90/10, 50/50, or transitional bilingual models. • Asset-Based Biliteracy Builds on the literacy skills students already bring. Decodable chapter books offer structured practice for decoding and fluency in Spanish, while building parallel skills in English. Ideal for independent reading, partner work, or small groups. • Promotes Cross-linguistic Transfer Decoding skills learned in Spanish transfer to English, strengthening reading in both languages while building academic language, vocabulary, comprehension, and oral language in both Spanish and English, creating a clear, coordinated pathway to biliteracy. 14

Differentiated Instruction: One Program Across All Tiers of Support PAF Reading Program is intentionally designed to meet the diverse needs of learners. It is taught in groups of students with similar skills who can move at a similar pace. This enables teachers to accelerate stronger students and spend more time with those who require more support. As a result, PAF Reading Program can be used across all tiers, with pacing, group size, setting, and intensity adjusted to meet students’ needs. This effective approach provides a consistent and cohesive program to meet all students’ needs and support their learning with a strong sense of continuity. Curriculum-Based Assessment Offered in Print & Digitally • Assess digitally, in minutes. Give and score the Test of Single Word Reading (TSWR) right in the Assessment Management Tool, for both placement and progress monitoring. • Place every student with confidence. Built-in placement guidance removes all gueswork. • See growth at a glance. Individual and group reports show exactly where each student stands. • Get time back. No paper tests, no hand-scoring, more time for teaching. • Build smarter small groups. Data-driven grouping puts every student in the right place for instruction. 17

4 Professional Learning The goal of PAF’s professional development is to ensure effective instruction by teachers and successful reading outcomes for students. Our team will work with you to make sure you have everything you need to implement the program successfully and with integrity. We start with a general conversation to learn about your school or district, your student population, and your literacy goals. We design a partnership that will ensure the program is effective in your setting. We will be by your side through the first year of implementation to advise you as you begin instruction. In addition to offering individual coaching sessions, we will provide guidance on important topics such as lesson planning, administering and analyzing assessments, and how to differentiate instruction. Consultation Ongoing Support Coursework & Workshops Continued Mentorship Training begins with a 12-hour course, focusing on PAF’s multisensory techniques for teaching reading, spelling, and handwriting in the primary grades. Topics include research-based instructional practices for developing accurate decoding and fluent reading through direct explicit instruction, building vocabulary and comprehension, lesson planning, and assessments. We pride ourselves on the relationships we build! Our dedicated master teachers are incredible resources who will be available to you throughout the first year of implementation and beyond. PAF offers monthly virtual office hours for teachers and adminitrators—no registration required! 18

Demonstrated Alignment with California Standards California Standards Alignment PAF Reading Program ensures all K–2 students master foundational skills as defined by the California ELA/ELD Framework, the California Common Core State Standards for ELA, and the Evaluation Criteria Map for Partial Program: Foundational Skills. PAF also meets California’s Standards for Evaluating Instructional Materials for Social Content. PAF provides systematic foundational skills instruction through authentic reading and writing activities, covering phonemic awareness, phonics, word recognition, morphology, spelling and decoding patterns, vocabulary, cohesive ties, handwriting, and comprehension strategies. Skills are taught in integrated lessons that reinforce one another, using decodable fiction and nonfiction, authentic literature, and informational text that grow in complexity to develop fluency, comprehension, and critical thinking.
